about: The court cards and jokers of Kit.card (cards/*.webp), drawn in the English pattern: the courts of a standard Bicycle or Waddingtons deck, which English card makers simplified from the Rouen woodblock pattern of the 1500s. scripts/cards/gen.py makes a picture from these: the style (jstyle for the joker), the card's brief and the tail; the black-and-white joker (JKB) is an edit of the color joker (JK) with bw. scripts/cards/pack.py then prints it in the inks below (every pixel one of them, specks cleaned away) and crops and sizes it. "sx" is where the small set's closer crop is centered across the picture (0.5 when absent), so what the figure holds stays in it. "pip" is the top corner of a court's half picture left plain for the suit sign, which kit.css prints there. "used" is the exact prompt of the picture now in the game.
style: The upper half of a court card of the English pattern of playing cards, the traditional design printed on a standard Bicycle or Waddingtons deck, which descends from the Rouen woodblock cards of the sixteenth century. Drawn exactly as such a card is printed: a woodblock print colored by stencil. Every shape is outlined by a bold, even, solid black line, and inside each outline is one flat, solid ink. No shading, no gradients, no highlights, no texture, no hatching, no cross-hatching and no brush marks anywhere. Only these inks, on plain white paper: black, a bright scarlet red, a golden yellow, a deep royal blue, and a pale flesh tone used only for the face, the neck and the hands. No other colors: no green, no purple, no brown, no grey, no orange, no pink, no light blue. The face is stylized and symmetrical like the face on a printed playing card: a smooth flat flesh area outlined in black, almond-shaped eyes drawn in black line, each with a round black pupil, thin arched black brows, a long nose drawn in a single line, a small red mouth, hair drawn as rows of black-outlined curls or locks filled with flat yellow or black, any beard or moustache the same. The pose is stiff, upright and formal. The robes are covered in rows and bands of small repeating ornament in the same inks, as on the traditional court cards: rows of dots and circles, scallops, rosettes of four round petals, zigzags, chevrons, lozenges, checks and stripes, a broad patterned collar, borders of jewels. No trefoils and no three-lobed shapes: nothing in the robe, the collar or the crown is shaped like a heart, a club or a spade. The headgear has simple flat-colored points, crosses, fleurs-de-lis or pearls. Composition: the figure is seen from the top of the headgear down to the middle of the chest, and the bottom edge of the picture cuts straight across the chest and arms, so that a copy turned upside down can join it there: the robe and the arms run right off the bottom edge, with no white band and no line under them. The figure fills the picture: the top of the headgear is just below the top edge, the shoulders and arms reach the left and right edges, and the face is large, in the upper middle of the picture. Graphic, flat, bold and decorative, exactly the look of a printed playing card from about 1890: not a modern illustration, not a cartoon, not anime, no 3D, no realistic modelling.
jstyle: A jester for the Joker of an English deck of playing cards from about 1890, in the same style as the English-pattern court cards: a woodblock print colored by stencil. Every shape is outlined by a bold, even, solid black line, and inside each outline is one flat, solid ink. No shading, no gradients, no highlights, no texture, no hatching and no brush marks anywhere. Only these inks, on plain white paper: black, a bright scarlet red, a golden yellow, a deep royal blue, and a pale flesh tone used only for the face and the hands. No other colors: no green, no purple, no brown, no grey, no orange, no pink. The face is stylized like the face on a printed playing card, outlined in black, with almond-shaped eyes, arched brows, a long nose drawn in one line and a small red mouth. His costume is covered in bands of small repeating ornament in the same inks: rows of dots, diamonds, scallops, zigzags and checks. Graphic, flat, bold and decorative: not a modern illustration, not a cartoon, not anime, no 3D, no realistic modelling. The whole picture is the figure on plain white paper: no ground line, no shadow, no scenery.
tail: Correct anatomy: every hand shown has five fingers drawn simply, in natural proportion to the head; anything held is held by its grip in a closed hand, in a way a person could really hold it, and it is one straight, solid object. Nothing but the figure and what the brief says he or she holds. No text, no letters, no numbers, no suit symbols (no hearts, diamonds, clubs or spades), no card border, no frame, no corner ornaments, no second figure.
bw: Redraw this exact picture, keeping the same jester, the same pose, the same face, the same patterns and every line in the same place, printed in black ink alone on white paper: every outline stays bold solid black, and each area that was colored becomes either plain white or solid black, or white filled with a small pattern of black dots, stripes or checks, so the two halves of his costume and his cap still read apart. Only black and white: no grey, no color at all. No text, no border.

KH.brief: The King of Hearts, the 'suicide king'. A king with long wavy yellow hair to his shoulders and a short yellow beard on his chin and jaw, but no moustache: his upper lip is bare (he is the one king without a moustache). His face is full face to the viewer, turned only slightly toward the viewer's left, and both of his eyes show. His right hand (on the viewer's left) is raised high beside his head, its fist holding the hilt of a straight sword; the long, broad blade, filled with flat royal blue and outlined in black so it stands out against his yellow hair, runs from that fist down diagonally behind his head, passing behind the back of his skull, so that it looks as if the sword is going into his head, and the blade's last third and its point show again past the far side of his head, against the white paper. A tall gold crown with crosses and red and blue jewels. Red robe with a blue and yellow patterned collar. The top right corner of the picture, a square a fifth of the picture's width, is plain white paper with nothing in it.

KD.brief: The King of Diamonds, 'the man with the axe', one of the one-eyed royals. He is drawn in strict side profile, like a head on a coin: his face points to the viewer's left, his nose points at the left edge, and only ONE eye shows. Neat yellow hair, a short pointed yellow beard and a curled moustache. His battle-axe is behind him, its blade facing toward him, as on the traditional card: the long straight shaft runs straight up near the right edge of the picture, behind his far shoulder and well clear of the back of his head; the broad axe head is fixed at the top of the shaft and reaches LEFT from the shaft, toward the back of his head, so that its curved cutting edge faces the back of his head and crown and the flat back of the axe head is against the shaft on the right. Nothing of the axe head reaches to the right of the shaft. His hand is not in front of him: no hand shows in front of his chest. A gold crown with points. Blue and red robe with yellow patterned bands. The top left corner of the picture, in front of his face, a square a fifth of the picture's width, is plain white paper with nothing in it.

KC.brief: The King of Clubs. A stout king with a full, square yellow beard and a curled moustache, his face in three-quarter view turned a little toward the viewer's right, both of his eyes showing clearly. In his hand on the viewer's left he holds a round gold orb with a small cross on top, at chest height. His other hand, on the viewer's right, holds the hilt of a sword whose straight blade rests upright against his shoulder. A heavy gold crown with points and crosses. Blue robe with red and yellow patterned bands and a black-and-white checked border. The top left corner of the picture, a square a fifth of the picture's width, is plain white paper with nothing in it.

JK.brief: The Joker: a court jester standing and facing the viewer, seen whole from the top of his cap down to his shoes, a slim upright figure in the middle of the picture. A sharp, amused face with a grin, both eyes showing. A fool's cap with exactly three floppy points (one falling to the left, one rising in the middle and curling over, one falling to the right) and a round yellow bell at the tip of each point, a pointed collar with a bell at each point, and particolored motley: one side red and one side blue, with yellow diamonds and black bands, striped hose, pointed shoes. In his right hand he holds a marotte (a short stick topped with a small jester's head in a cap) upright in front of his chest, close to his body; his left hand rests on his hip with the elbow tucked in. The whole figure, the marotte and both elbows included, fits inside the middle half of the picture's width, with wide plain white paper on both sides.
